question: GQ-001
subject: my own fix disabled the feature it was protecting, and I only found out by measuring it

the_first_fix_was_bad.what: a term-frequency budget: skip the modern index when a term is too common to exclude cheaply
the_first_fix_was_bad.what_it_actually_was: SEVENTEEN of twenty classic long-s words exceeded the budget — such, those, first, present, cause, himself, house, sense, disease, surface, distance, possible, vessel, season, phosphorus, instrument, passage
the_first_fix_was_bad.meaning: the modern index was disabled for 85% of the queries it exists to serve. That is switching the feature off, not trading it.

how_i_caught_it: I wrote "a real loss of long-s recall" in the worklog and then measured how large the loss was instead of leaving it as an assertion

the_real_fix.key_fact: passage_modern and passage_ext_search assign the SAME ROWID to the same passage — verified at rowid 500, antislaverydisun00unse:40 in both
the_real_fix.consequence: no cross-index set operation is needed: for each modern hit, look up that rowid in the printed index CONTENT TABLE, an ordinary B-tree
the_real_fix.per_term_not_phrase: FTS matching "electromagnetic induction" means both words appear anywhere; literal phrase-LIKE finds only adjacency. Measured FTS 10, phrase-LIKE 2, per-term-LIKE 10 — the phrase form would have admitted 8 duplicates
the_real_fix.candidate_cap: LIMIT bounds rows RETURNED, which bounds nothing for a stopword: "the" matches 2,723,718 modern rows and nearly all also print "the", so the join walked millions to find 3 (58s). Capping CANDIDATES at 40,000 is safe in a way the frequency budget was not — every candidate is still tested by the same exclusion, so whatever it finds is exactly correct.

the_same_mistake_twice_in_one_file: I put a BACKTICK inside a template-literal comment, breaking the whole script — for the SECOND time today. Both times every query returned 0 hits in ~40ms, which reads as speed until you look.
